title: Self-supervised learning for neural topic models with variance-invariance-covariance regularization
read_from: arXiv preprint 2502.09944 (published version: Knowledge and Information Systems)
task: Improving topic coherence of VAE-based NTMs
problem: Contrastive NTMs can suffer representation collapse and rely on heuristic positive sampling.
architecture: VICNTM: SCHOLAR-based NTM where latent topic representations of an anchor and its positive sample are regularised with variance, invariance and covariance terms (VICReg); variants with an expander to high-dimensional space and combinations with CLNTM; positive samples by tf-idf word replacement or a model-based adversarial augmentation.
key_results: k = 200 NPMI on 20NG: 0.3212 vs CLNTM 0.3187 and ECRTM 0.1811.
ECRTM has higher TD (e.g. IMDb 0.8812 vs 0.8448).
strengths: Brings collapse-preventing self-supervised regularisation to topic models; ten-seed evaluation.

limitations.text: tf-idf-based positive samples give limited diversity; adversarial augmentation is a simple first instance.
Gains over CLNTM are small (within one standard deviation in several cases).
